citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
During USDA facility inspection, two dogs were examined and found to have heavy dental tartar accumulation with
gingival erosions. Subsequent inspection of facility animal health records showed that these two dogs, “Oscar” (intact
male poodle, DOB 12-23-2019, USDA tag #56) and “Raven” (intact female Shih Tzu, USDA tag #68), had been previously
examined by the facility attending veterinarian on 06-16-2026. On the corresponding physical exam forms filled out by the
attending veterinarian, the attending veterinarian had recommended dentals be done. In conversation with the licensee,
no date had been scheduled for dental cleanings on these two dogs with the attending veterinarian.
Timely follow up and appropriate treatment of dental and other health issues with your veterinarian is essential for the
overall health and well-being of animals.
Each dealer shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include methods to prevent, control
and treat diseases and injuries.
Correct by August 04, 2026

APHIS 7005 Forms (Record of Acquisition of Dogs and Cats on Hand) are incomplete and missing required USDA
information.
1) Blocks 1,2,3 and 4 and the block containing the licensee’s USDA license number have not been filled out on the forms
2) There are seven dogs listed (Payton, Amber, Oscar, Misty, Cruella, Tippy and Marly) which are missing required ID
numbers under block A of the forms.
3) There are eight dogs listed (Sugar, Vanna, Payton, Tippy, Marly, Lucy, Oscar and Misty) which are missing required
acquisition information under block I of the forms. Although the blocks have been filled with the names of the persons or
entities from which the dogs were acquired, these entries are missing a required address, USDA license
number/registration number, or driver’s license number with State and vehicle license number with State of the individuals
from whom the dogs were acquired.
Entering required 7005 form information, including addresses and license or registration numbers of persons from which
animals are acquired, is needed for animal traceability. Animal traceability is essential in helping USDA personnel and
other animal health professionals contain and track animal diseases and prevent unlawful animal activity.
Each dealer is required to keep and maintain records that include the names and addresses, the USDA license or
registration numbers (if licensed or registered), or the driver’s license numbers and vehicle license numbers of those
persons from which dogs are acquired.
Correct by August 04. 2026

Inside the whelping building an empty syringe was found on the floor near the south door along with an open container of
fly bait, a dog collar, and an empty vaccine vial. On the bottom of the open storage cabinet along the south wall there was
an accumulation of dirt and debris, empty syringe wrappers, a propane cannister and old flood light bulb. Next to the west
side of the cabinet there was another propane cannister lying on the floor, along with two plastic dog doors, and a piece of
pvc pipe.
Clutter and accumulations of trash and discarded materials on the floor and inside the storage cabinet hinder adequate
cleaning and sanitation and provide a refuge for pests and vermin.
Animal housing areas must be kept neat and free of clutter; and free of trash, junk, waste materials, and other items and
materials not associated with facility cleaning or animal husbandry.
Correct this date forward

The gate panel of an exterior occupied run located on the south side of the main kennel building has corrosion along the
bottom horizontal cross member. Additionally, the bottom of the adjoining southwest vertical support of the gate panel has
corroded through and has exposed sharp edges.
Corroded surfaces are difficult to adequately sanitize and can compromise the structural integrity of enclosures. Rusted
and exposed sharp edges are also a potential injury hazard to dogs occupying the run.
Housing surfaces in contact with dogs must be free of excessive rust that prevents cleaning and sanitation or that affects
the structural strength of the surface. Surfaces also must be free of jagged edges or sharp points that might injure
animals.
Correct by July 29, 2026

During inspection inside the whelping building there were two bags of calf milk replacer in direct contact with the floor.
One of the bags, located in the southeast corner, was open and had visible cobwebs at the top along with debris and
powdered milk replacer inside the bag.
During inspection inside the main kennel building there was also found a bag of open adult dog food.
It is important to store open bags of food in leakproof and closed containers to prevent contamination and pest infiltration.
Unopened bags of food should be stored off the floor to facilitate floor cleaning, prevent vermin infestation and to prevent
food spoilage from moisture seepage from the floor into food bags.
All supplies of food must be stored off the floor and away from walls. Open supplies of food must be contained in
leakproof containers with tight fitting lids to prevent contamination and spoilage.
Correct this date forward.

A buildup of debris and grime was observed on the interior of two galvanized self feeders in occupied runs inside the main
kennel building.
A buildup of debris and grime on the interior of feeders can lead to bacterial overgrowth and hasten food spoilage.
Food receptacles must be kept clean and sanitized in accordance with regulations under 3.11 (b).
Correct this date forward

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
Along the ground adjacent to the north side of whelping building there are two snow shovels on the ground along with
various pieces of litter and part of a broken enclosure. There is also an overgrowth of weeds in contact with the exterior
wall.
Along the ground adjacent to the west side of the whelping building there is a plastic lid, spray nozzle, various trash debris
and a lawnmower underneath the suspended enclosures.
Along the ground adjacent to the east side of the whelping building there is various trash debris, including an old shoe,
carboard box, and empty can underneath the suspended enclosures. There is also a mop and various trash debris on the
ground near the dumpster close to the southeast corner exterior of the whelping building.
Along the exterior of the main kennel there is an overgrowth of vegetation/weeds adjacent to the northeast exterior run
and east building wall.
Accumulations of trash, junk or other discarded items and overgrowth of weeds prevent effective premise cleaning and
sanitation and also increase breeding grounds and cover for pests and rodents.
Premises must be kept free of accumulations of trash, junk and discarded matter. Weeds and vegetation must be
controlled to facilitate premise cleaning, control pests and to protect the health and well-being of animals.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
Inside the whelping building there was an accumulation of dead flies on the south window sill, on the floor near the south
door, and in a fly bait station located on floor by the south door. Outside the whelping building there were dozens of live
flies observed on the building exterior east wall and on the adjacent ground underneath enclosures, as well as on exterior
contact surfaces of occupied enclosures. On the south exterior end of the main kennel, there were also a large number of
live flies observed landing on the concrete and exterior walls of occupied runs. The large number of dead and live flies
observed during inspection indicates that current pest control measures are inadequate to control fly infestation.
Flies can be vectors for animal disease and may cause animals undue stress due to bites and annoyance. In addition to
indicating inadequate pest control measures, infestations may also be linked to waste and manure management issues
and/or insanitary conditions around a facility.
An effective program for pest control must be established and maintained so as to promote the health and well-being of
animals and reduce pest contamination of the premises.
Correct by July 29, 2026

The facility’s current written Program of Veterinary Care is incomplete. Under Section IV. Vaccination, Parasite Control
and Prevention, there are no entries under block A listing the types of vaccines and frequency or schedule of vaccinations
to be administered to adult dogs in the kennel, or for puppies older than 8 weeks. Also, under the rabies vaccination
block, the only schedule entry states “when old enough.”
Having and following a veterinarian approved written schedule of vaccinations for all dogs in the facility is essential for
animal health and prevention of disease within the facility.
The written program of veterinary care must include vaccinations for all dogs in the kennel against contagious and/or
deadly diseases and be in accordance with a schedule approved by the attending veterinarian.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
Additional Inspectors:
Margaret Shaver, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
